owaspChecklist.A09_logging_monitoring: pass — three distinct admin-alert codes (E031 host-rejected, E032 fetch-error, E033 no-body); ERROR-level log via _notify; oversize-body case has WARN log with size + URL

findings.title: allow_redirects=True (default) lets the allowlisted host redirect to an attacker-controlled host
findings.description: session.get() at line 120-124 uses the requests default allow_redirects=True. If t-hunted.blogspot.com (or an intermediary in Blogger's CDN) ever returns a 3xx Location pointing at an external/internal host, urllib3 will follow without re-validating the destination against _ALLOWED_HOSTS. The bypass requires either (a) Blogger account takeover of t-hunted.blogspot.com or (b) a future Blogger feature that lets posters emit arbitrary 3xx Location headers — both are low-likelihood, but the cost of disabling redirects is one keyword argument. Project convention in lamley_source.py also omits this hardening, so this is a systemic minor rather than task-specific.
findings.impact: Theoretical SSRF bypass after a redirect; with Blogger's actual behavior today the issue is unreachable.
findings.recommendation: Add allow_redirects=False, or follow redirects manually and re-validate each hop's host with _is_allowed_t_hunted_url: `response = session.get(link, timeout=_TIMEOUT_SECONDS, headers={'User-Agent': _USER_AGENT}, allow_redirects=False)` and, if a 3xx is received, resolve Location relative to the original URL and re-check the allowlist before re-issuing. Apply project-wide for consistency with lamley_source.

findings.title: _MAX_BYTES check runs only after the full body has been downloaded into memory
findings.description: Line 133 reads `len(response.content)` AFTER `session.get(...)` has already buffered the entire response. A hostile or misbehaving upstream (e.g., compromised CDN edge for t-hunted.blogspot.com, or an upstream HTTP smuggling scenario) could send a multi-GB body and exhaust process memory before the 2 MB cap takes effect. The cap currently functions only as a 'drop oversized garbage before BeautifulSoup' filter — not as a DoS guard.
findings.impact: Memory-exhaustion DoS on the bot process if upstream sends arbitrarily large body. Low likelihood for Blogger but non-zero.
findings.recommendation: Use streamed download with manual size enforcement: `response = session.get(link, timeout=_TIMEOUT_SECONDS, headers={'User-Agent': _USER_AGENT}, stream=True); chunks=[]; total=0; for chunk in response.iter_content(65536): total += len(chunk); if total > _MAX_BYTES: response.close(); logger.warning(...); return None; chunks.append(chunk); body = b''.join(chunks)`. Defer if you intentionally match lamley_source's pattern (then carry a project-wide TODO).

findings.title: Full untrusted URL echoed verbatim in admin-alert / log strings without length cap or sanitization
findings.description: Lines 115, 129, 136-139, 164 pass the caller-supplied `link` through `admin_alerts.alert_t_hunted_*` and `logger.warning` unmodified. A hostile RSS feed could craft a multi-kilobyte URL containing control characters or Telegram-MarkdownV2 metacharacters that mangle the admin alert rendering, or simply blow up the alert channel with noise. Same pattern as lamley_source so systemic — but worth flagging because Task 2's E031-E033 builders will land next and should escape/truncate at the boundary.
findings.impact: Admin-channel UX degradation; not exploitable for code execution.
findings.recommendation: In admin_alerts.alert_t_hunted_* (Task 2), truncate link to ~200 chars and escape Telegram MarkdownV2 special chars before embedding. No change needed in t_hunted_source.py itself.

positiveFindings: SSRF allowlist uses Python tuple-membership on `urlparse(...).hostname.lower()` — the textbook-correct primitive; rejects all four required negative cases (userinfo, suffix, subdomain, foreign netloc) plus loopback/link-local/AWS-metadata.
Fail-closed: any parse error → False; missing hostname → '' → not in tuple. No exception escapes _is_allowed_t_hunted_url.
Scheme allowlist (http/https) blocks file://, javascript:, data:, gopher://, ftp:// — explicitly tested.
Network short-circuit verified by test asserting session.get is NOT called on host rejection.
Regex `=s\d+(-c)?(?:/|$)` is bounded, non-nested, ReDoS-safe (50k digit run sub'd in <0.2 ms).
HTML parsed with html.parser (stdlib), not lxml — no XXE/RCE surface from BeautifulSoup backend.
<script>/<style>/<noscript> tags decomposed before text extraction — XSS-via-text-content vector closed for downstream renderers.
Timeout pinned at 15 s; UA is generic non-credential string; no eval/exec/subprocess/pickle/yaml.load.
No secrets in source — module imports admin_alerts but contains no API keys, tokens, or connection strings.
Notifier failure isolated: _notify wraps notifier(message) in try/except so an alert-channel outage cannot break the parser.
